technical_and_design_decisions: Use Java 17+ as required by Spring Framework 6.0 for development compatibility.
Leverage existing Spring XD infrastructure and APIs for stream management and lifecycle operations.
Implement resource cleanup (U1, U2) using Spring's lifecycle callbacks and message bus integration to ensure proper teardown of queues/topics.
Utilize Spring Integration's wiretap functionality for tracing features (U6) as referenced in the specification.
Extend stream creation and deployment mechanisms to support side channels (U7) by adding optional channel parameters.
Design manifest file loading (U4) to support common formats like .properties and .xml, with robust error handling.
Ensure backward compatibility and configurability for all new features to maintain existing system stability.
Develop reference architectures (U5) as modular Spring XD configurations and documentation for easy adoption.
Implement taxi trips analysis (U8) as a standalone Spring XD stream application using real-time event processing.
Adopt an agile development approach with iterative testing and integration for each user story.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD codebase is available and can be modified without major restructuring.
A development environment with Java 17+, Spring XD, and necessary build tools (e.g., Maven, Gradle) is pre-configured.
All user stories (U1-U8) are prioritized and will be fully implemented in this software increment.
No significant changes to external dependencies or libraries are required beyond standard updates.
Testing will be conducted on a dedicated test environment with mock data and simulated message bus resources.
Documentation will be created as part of the development process, covering both technical and user aspects.
The team has access to Spring XD documentation and community resources for guidance on integration points.
Time estimates account for common development tasks like code reviews, pair programming, and debugging.

activities.activity_description: Analyze all user stories (U1-U8), gather detailed requirements, define system interfaces, and design overall solution architecture, including impact on existing Spring XD components.
Develop and integrate functionality to clean up message bus resources (e.g., queues, topics) and stale resources when streams are destroyed, addressing U1 and U2 through lifecycle management hooks.
Add capability to edit deployed or undeployed streams without destruction, by extending stream management APIs to support property updates, as specified in U3.
Develop feature to load deployment manifests from external files (e.g., .properties, .xml) and integrate with stream deployment process, reducing manual inline property entry per U4.
Create reference architectures, sample configurations, and documentation for field engineers to build proof-of-concepts using Spring XD, capturing domain-specific ideas as per U5.
Add optional trace deployment properties for modules in streams to enable logging and notifications, using Spring Integration wiretap functionality, as detailed in U6.
Develop functionality to create optional side channels within streams for tracing and tracking module progress, extending stream channel creation as per U7.
Implement a proof-of-concept stream application to study New York City taxi trips using Spring XD, evaluating event-based systems for real-time analytics as per U8.
Conduct comprehensive testing including unit tests, integration tests, and system tests for all implemented features to ensure functionality, performance, and reliability.
Prepare user guides, API documentation, deployment manuals, and configuration guidelines for the software increment, facilitating smooth adoption and maintenance.
